scope_note: A strong, independent female cahracter that is central to the story.
example: Lara Croft from *Tomb Raider* and Bayonetta from *Bayonetta*

scope_note: This male character often appears the same across many different games. For example, in many games there is a white male charactter with a buzz-cut and a strong jawline.

This is a character driven by the quest to discover new lands, dieas, people, and experiences. This is different from The Conquerer in that they do not need to possess the new item, location, or idea. The experience is often enough.
example: The protagonists of *Uncharted Waters*, specifically Ernst.

scope_note: A character whose motivating factor is to collect all of something.
A character whose motivating factor is to create or construct something, typically physical. This is often an empire or civilization that might also be for their private use.
example: Some individual playing *Minecraft* and the Prince from Katamari Damacy.

scope_note: A character with relentless persistence and unyielding determination, often pushing through extreme adversity or impossible odds without giving up.
example: Naruto from *Naruto Shippuden: Ultimate Ninja Storm 4* and Phoenix Wright from *Ace Attorney*.

scope_note: A person who spend most of their time in the outdoors and who is proficient at hunting, tracking, and wilderness survival.
example: Anden Goodmanner from *A Dance with Rogues*.

scope_note: This character has no exceptional abilities.
This character has been chosen by their people or divine beings to make a difference in the world.
A character that does not want to take an active role in the story, but finds they should or must.
example: Chun Li from the *Street Fighter* franchise.

scope_note: Police or police-like figures that use questionable or subversive methods to investifate possible crimes against the state or the main authority.
An individual whose job it is to coordinate and gather information. Often an indispensible ally.
Money buys power. And power often corrupts.
example: The *Mario* series generally features wealthy, evil royalty.

scope_note: This cahracter may or may not have powers, but he/she/it is the main antagonist of the story. This is usually the final boss in a game. Defeating The Big Bad will make the hero triumphant.
This character takes pleasure in making their pupil suffer. An example could be a particularly mean drill sergeant.
This character is someone related to the main character or a trusted family friend or advisor. They represent a threat to the main character.

This character cannot achieve their goals within legal or moral restrictions, so they reluctantly take matters into their own hands. Conversely, they may also be following laws or moral restrictions to the letter, despite reservations.
A character who operates outside of the law for good or evil.
example: the main character from *Red Dead Redemption*.

scope_note: This character is a young child or adolescent that may or may not actually be creepy, but they project a creepy or unusual demeanor. Unlike the Deadly child, they may not be violent or skilled.
This character is a young child or adolescent that may not seem dangerous at first glance, but they are either formidable fighters or have supernatural powers.
example: The children who live in Little Lamplight in *Fallout 3* and Annie from *League of Legends*.

scope_note: This character has no parents or guardians to keep them in place when they are first introduced to the player.
example: Ellie from *The Last of Us*, Squall from *Final Fantasy 8*.

scope_note: This character has no memory of events that took place immediately before the start of the story.
example: Dust from *Dust: An Elysian Tail*, the main character of *Amnesia: The Dark Descent*.

scope_note: This character was once a human or human-like life form that was changed into an animal or monster that may be misunderstood by other characters.
example: Kronos from *Kronos God of War* or any werewolf characters.

scope_note: A character that is from an underworld and represents a greater evil.
The character that is the highest member of an evil hierarchy, often from the underworld.
This character is a creature that has never been seen before, like Cthulhu.
example: The Reapers from the *Mass Effect* franchise.

scope_note: This character possesses knowledge or has access to something that the main characters need to move forward in the story.
example: Faralda from *The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim*.

scope_note: This is a character or characters that were once inanimate and then activated by another character.
example: The colossi in *Shadow of the Colossus*.

scope_note: This character may be a voice heard over an intercom or a supernatural being.
Any undead or otherwise supernaturally animated creature that was once alive.
A person with noble lineage who skirts responsibility or wants to be free from their responsibilities.
A character that may or may not be aware of their royal blood, but is hidden for one reason or another.
example: Alistair in *Dragon Age: Origins* and Zelda (as Sheik) from the *Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time*.

scope_note: This character may represent some sort of evil and controls a vast army of minions. They may or may not be the main antagonist.
A character whose primary objective is to possess and control lands, people, and resources in order to increase their power.
A person in charge of a combat unit or armed forces.
example: Commander Shepard from the Mass Effect franchise.

scope_note: A creature that accompanies the main character throughout the story.
example: Cedric the Owl from *King’s Quest V*.

scope_note: An individual character or group of small creatures that work for a particular individual and their ultimate goal.
example: The Tonberry and Moogle from the *Final Fantasy* franchise.

scope_note: A character that has experienced combat and that experience of combat is formative to their personality.
A character that is due to be sacrificed to a greater cause either by divine prophecy or as collateral damage.
A commonly encountered and dispensable enemy employed by the antagonist character operating individually or in a larger group.
example: The Storm Troopers from the *Star Wars* franchise.

scope_note: Characters who are held captive by the antagonist in order to leverage the protagonist into doing the bidding of the antagonist. They generally require rescue.
example: Promo Girl from the Resident *Evil 3: Nemesis* during Operation: Mad Jackal.

scope_note: A character that is not immediately perceived as useful and relied on by a storyteller for comic relief. However, their guidance or assistance for a quest makes them indispensable.
example: Navi from Legend of *Zelda: Ocarina Of Time*

scope_note: An individual chosen by divine intervention for some higher purpose. This purpose may include acting as a 'fifth element' (a physical embodiment of a concept) or host.
A character who rules the underworld.
example: The Seven Great Evils in the *Diablo* series.

scope_note: A small icon or creature that assists a character throughout their story and may offer special skills to a player such as enhancing an attack.
example: Navi from *Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time* and Pix from *League of Legends*.

scope_note: A character that mediates another character’s morality.
A character who is perpetually in danger due to their innocence or naiveté and they are usually saved by the protagonist.
A character who is believed to be evil at the beginning of the story, though investigation or new information is actually revealed to be an ally or 'good guy.'
example: No example provided for this due to possible spoilers. Proceed with caution when assigning this trope.

scope_note: A group of people outside of the main society that usually live without technology and operate on a tribal system of governance.
An individual or group of characters that holds a philosophical belief that everyone must be similar or the same.
example: The Geth from *Mass Effect* or The Borg from *Star Trek* franchise

scope_note: An individual or group of characters driven solely by the strength of their beliefs in politics or religion to the point of which they try to convert anyone to their point of view.
An individual or group of characters that go against the ideological flow of a larger group with possible risks to their well being.
An individual or small group of characters that believe they must stay separate from a larger population.
example: The Mages' Collective from Dragon Age and the Gerudo tribe from *Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time*

scope_note: A group or individual whose primary goal is to change the status quo.
example: The Alliance from the *Star Wars* franchise.

scope_note: An individual or group of characters that steal large quantities of goods (government or private property), usually on some sort of large transport vessel.
example: The pirates from *The Pirates of the Caribbean* franchise.

scope_note: An individual or group of characters that come from a different world or time.
example: The Four Masks from Shadow Hearts

scope_note: Typically an army or gathering that has strength in numbers and are enemy or other to the main protagonists.
example: Orcs from The Lord of the Rings franchise

scope_note: A character that is quick to fight and often has a short temper.
A wizard, witch, or other character that has supernatural powers.

A character that uses methods that are based in gendered stereotypes (i.e. fighting with a skillet). This character may also have extreme flexibility or unlikely acrobatics and may have physically revealing fighting styles that male characters would not employ in order for the storyteller or game designer to show off the female body.
example: Momoko from *The King of Fighters*, commonly seen in arcade style fighting games such as *Soul Calibur*, *Street Fighter*, *Mortal Kombat*, etc.

scope_note: A character that is the target of assault and sustains the most damage during battle. Often they are used strategically to draw attention away from weaker characters so they can pursue their own directives.
A character that employs stealth, dirty fighting, and agile techniques to inflict the most damage on enemies while avoiding taking damage themselves.
A character distinguished by her dark hair, often depicted as emotionally distant and mysterious.
This character may seem formidable based on its appearance, but it is actually an ally.
A character with white or silver hair who is ruthless and malevolent, in contrast to their striking appearance.
A character who is portrated as stereotypically attractice but lacking in intelligence.
A character who is overweight and portrated in a negative light.
A male head of a family or tribe.
example: Sun Jian in the *Dynast Warriors* series.

scope_note: The female head of a family or tribe.

term: The Girl in the Boys Club
scope_note: The female character in the stroy or game that embodies typically masculine traits.
A cute, diminutive character that packs a powerful punch or has a prickly personality.
example: Kirby from the *Kirby* franchise and Shantotto from *Final Fantasy XI*.

scope_note: A female character that is deadly and often has a tragic backstory.
The single female character in the story or game of all male characters.
example: Of the four playable characters in *Borderlands*, onyl one is female.

scope_note: A female character whose sole reason of existence is to enliven the life of (a usually male) character.
A female version of a cahracter that was originally male.
example: Ms. Pac Man and Toadette from the *Mario* franchise.

scope_note: When female characters are depicted in games only as objects to be rescued, sexually pursued, or protected and otherwise serves no function in the narrative.
example: Any sex worker or groupie in *Saints Row* or women in the *Grand Theft Auto* franchise.

scope_note: When there is only one black person in a cast of otherwise white characters.
When the Asian character is really good with STEM subjects to the exclusion of other skills, particularly social skills.
When an indigenous character has a connection or powers relating to the Earth or animals and this is usually an inherited trait from a tribe or their ancestry.
When a character is of alien origins is meant to represent an analog to real-world ethnicities or races and these real-world ethnicities or races to not appear in the universe otherwise.
example: The Syreen from *Star Control 2* and several races from the *Mass Effect* franchise.

scope_note: A form of 'blackspotation' that simultaneously sexualized and defeminizes a black female character.
Typically a large individual who is paired with a young child with the 'badass' providing protection and support for the child.
example: Corvo Attano and Emily Kaldwin from *Dishonor*.

scope_note: When two characters compliment each other in terms of physical appearance or personalities. One is often more serious than the other.
example: Fia and Lian in *Riviera: The Promised Land*.

scope_note: Two to three individuals aligned with the antagonists that cannot seem to agree on anything.
A team of four individuals who all compliment each other in appearance, skills, and/or fighting styles.
example: The Black, White, Red, and Yellow birds from *Angry Birds*.

scope_note: A group of characters who, despite not being biologically related, form deep, supportive bonds that provide emotional connection, belonging, and mutual care, often overcoming shared struggles or challenges together.
example: The Straw Hat crew in *One Piece: World Seeker*, The Shepherds in *Fire Emblem Awakening*.

scope_note: When a character changes their alliance unexpectedly and sticks with their choice.
When a character struggles with the desire to connect with others despite them being a food source for them.
When a character takes action that negatively impacts others to achieve a percieved 'greater good'.
A character so pure and perfect that they cannot live in this world and thus they get killed, often driving the main character to greater feats of heroics on their behalf.
When a character or group of characters is presented with a lose-lose choice from their foe (i.e., choose between two loves ones).
When a character needs or soothes a creature that would normally intend harm in order to get past them.
When a character or group of characters needs to create something in order to move forward with the story.
When a character or characters must find their way through a maze or maze-like setting.
When a character or gorup of characters needs to defeat a beast based on a request from the public or an individual or a serendipitious encounter.
When a character or team needs to lcoate a particular item, creature, or individual in order to move forward with the story.
This trope occurs when a character or a group of characters continually resues one particular character.
Sometimes unrelated characters band together because they were each wronged in a similar or different way by the same character.
When a character learns something important about their future or recieves a calling from a higher power.
When a character or group of characters is pulled into another dimention and needs to find a way home.
A large entity seems like an insurmountable foe, but a small group of resistance fighters come together to attempt to defeat them.
When two characters enhance their powers by joining their efforts or physical items to create a larger item. Sometimes this can also mean a bond of a spiritual sort.
When two characters or teams from opposing sides join forces to defeat a common foe.
When two or more characters were once allies, but events in the past have pushed them apart to the point at which they are now enemies.
At the climax of the story, everything seems hopeless.
At the climax of the story, this last-ditch effort made by the protagonists or teammates to overcome their trials. It often accompanies a 'this is so crazy it might just work' type of plan.
At the climax of the story, one of the main characters sacrifices themselves to save others.
At the climax of the story, one of the characters that the players thought was dead (or nearly dead) delivers a mortal wound to their opponent, often saving another indiviual in the process.

At the climax, once revenge has been achieved for a character for whom it was the driving force, new information comes to light that renders the revenge unethical or unnecessary even though it has already happened.
At the end of the story, one of the characters chooses to stay in the new setting instead of going home with their teammates (if they have any).
At the end of the story, one of the main protagonists leaves the group after their ordeal is over.
At the end of the game the players are unsure of the ending- it could go multiple ways.
